items.summary: Georgia released 16 Turkish football fans on Friday after police detained them during clashes at a match between Turkey’s Beşiktaş and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er-Sheva in the Black Sea city of Batumi, Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said. Thursday’s Europa League match was briefly suspended after clashes in the stands. items.title: Russian Navy to receive five missile-carrying submarines by 2030 — Putin
items.summary: Russia intends to continue developing and improving the Navy, including its submarine forces, the head of state underscored

items.title: Putin describes nuclear-powered sub Perm as weapon of global scale
items.summary: The president stressed that Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building such powerful nuclear-powered submarines

items.title: Ukraine's Azov announces 'Hell-3' operation, destroys Russian fuel depot in occupied Donetsk Oblast
items.summary: Russian forces had concealed the fuel depot and attempted to protect it with camouflage, electronic warfare systems and mobile fire groups, but the Ukrainian units managed to destroy both the storage site and its supporting logistics infrastructure, Azov said.

items.title: Zelensky chairs meeting on Kyiv situation attended by Klitschko
items.summary: During a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief’s Headquarters of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the logistics situation in Kyiv was discussed in the event of a significant deterioration of the situation due to Russian strikes. Among the speakers was the capital’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko.

items.title: Poland warns of anti-Ukrainian fake news regarding Ukrainian man who set himself on fire in Warsaw
items.summary: Warsaw police spokesperson Jakub Pacyniak warned on 27 November that false claims, fake farewell letters and conspiracy theories are circulating online to incite anti-Ukrainian sentiment after a 22-year-old Ukrainian man set himself on fire outside the Presidential Palace.

items.title: «Мы здесь все орки»
items.summary: 26 ноября Юрий Дудь выпустил интервью с Даниилом Туленковым — бывшим предпринимателем из Свердловской области, который полгода воевал против Украины, а после возвращения написал книгу «Шторм Z. У вас нет других нас». Сегодня Туленков говорит, что его устроило бы прекращение войны даже на условиях вывода российских войск из Украины, вместе с тем собирает деньги на дроны для бывших сослуживцев. items.title: By Putin's logic, Russia should be returned to Mongolia, Belarus' Lukashenka says
items.summary: The Belarusian leader said medieval history cannot justify territorial claims, since Russian lands were themselves once under Mongol rule, and traced East Slavic statehood to Kyivan Rus'. He then appeared to soften the remarks, saying Putin "perfectly understands this" and is "misinterpreted".

items.title: Spox Pletenchuk: Russia seeks alternative supply routes for troops after partial collapse of Kerch Bridge
items.summary: Following the damage to the Kerch Bridge, the Russian Federation is unable to fully supply Crimea with everything required by the Russian occupying forces; however, they will attempt to route more supplies overland.

items.title: ‘No reports, no strikes’: Russia’s pro-war bloggers slam proposed prison sentences for sharing photos and videos of Ukrainian attacks
items.summary: Yesterday, a group of Russian senators introduced a bill in the State Duma that calls for prison terms of up to five years for illegally distributing information about the aftermath of Ukrainian strikes, as well as terrorist attacks and sabotage. Bans on publishing photos and videos of attack aftermath are already in effect in many regions, though until now the punishment has only involved administrative fines. Now a new article could appear in the Criminal Code as well.…

items.title: Eurocontrol decides to extend operations of ATM Solidarity Fund for Ukraine for 2027-2028
items.summary: Eurocontrol member states have decided to extend the operations of the European ATM (Air Traffic Management) Voluntary Solidarity Fund for 2027-2028.

items.title: Russia has lost at least 87 members of its most secretive special forces unit since invading Ukraine, investigation finds
items.summary: At least 87 members of Russia’s Special Operations Forces (SSO) have died since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, iStories, an independent Russian investigative outlet, found after examining a leaked Rosstat database of death records.

items.title: Ukraine brings back 11 people from occupation and Russia, including children and deported Oleshky care home resident – photos
items.summary: Ukraine has brought back nine children from occupied Kherson, Zaporizhzhia and Crimea alongside two women, including deported Oleshky care home resident Anastasiia Mamotiuk, bringing repatriations assisted by Melania Trump to 40.

items.title: Russia Targets Military, Logistics Facilities in Ukraine
Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths
items.summary: After a series of Russian strikes and with the onset of winter cold, Ukraine was forced to halt all electricity exports, while imports reached their highest level since mid-June.
